newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures slip in line with weak bullion.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures slip in line with weak bullion.

text.p: Yen-denominated gold futures ended lower across the board on Tuesday, pressured by declines in spot gold prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from four to nine yen per gram weaker. The most-active August 1997 gold futures settled four yen per gram lower at 1,335 yen.
Bullion was quoted at $382.55/382.55 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $383.40/383.80 in New York on Monday.
"Spot gold was pounded down by selling interest from overseas investors, and Japanese trade houses sold gold futures in tandem with weaker spot gold," one trader said.
Traders said some physical buying was detected during Asian hours, but the buying was overwhelmed by selling pressure.
Sentiment in the gold market remained bearish.
"Although spot gold prices fell for nine consecutive days, the market has not hit bottom and gold is likely to slip further towards support at $380," the trader said.
Traders said talk about gold sales by the IMF were also partly responsible for weak gold prices.
In the gold futures market, views that the yen will not fall much against the dollar also helped trade houses build fresh short positions in distant months, they said.
Other precious metal futures settled weaker in sluggish trade.
Platinum futures ranged from one to four yen per gram easier. Benchmark August ended three yen lower at 1,367 yen after moving within a tight range throughout the day.
Silver prices ranged from 0.8 yen to 1.3 yen per 10 grams easier. Benchmark August was 1.3 yen lower at 180.7 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from unchanged to three yen per gram lower. Benchmark August was flat at 439 yen.
